issues.title: Session without context manager usage
issues.description: The rule requires all database sessions to use 'with Session(db.engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:' pattern for proper resource management, but the code creates a session without a context manager and never closes it
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
session = Session(db.engine)
row = session.scalar(stmt)
if not row:
    raise ConversationVariableNotFoundError("conversation variable not found in the database")
row.data = variable.model_dump_json()
session.commit()
issues.rule_name: SQLAlchemy Sessions Must Use Context Managers

issues.title: Database transaction commits called on every variable update instead of batched
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer now calls flush() inside the loop for each updated conversation variable, rather than batching all updates and flushing once after the loop completes. This causes multiple unnecessary database commits when multiple conversation variables are updated in a single node execution, significantly degrading performance and creating database contention. The original implementation correctly tracked whether any updates occurred with the `updated_any` flag and only flushed once after all updates were queued.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence layer registered before persistence layer causing event ordering issue
issues.description: The conversation_variable_layer is now registered before the persistence_layer in the graph engine layer stack. In event-driven architectures with layered middleware, the order of layer registration determines the order in which layers receive and process events. By registering conversation_variable_layer first, it will receive and process NodeRunSucceededEvent events before the persistence_layer has a chance to persist the node execution state. This creates a race condition where conversation variables might be updated in the database before the corresponding node execution is persisted, leading to data inconsistency if failures occur between the two operations.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence failures are silently ignored
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer calls update() without catching exceptions, relying on the graph engine's blanket exception handler which logs but continues execution. When persistence fails (e.g., database errors, ConversationVariableNotFoundError), the exception is caught by the engine's try-except in event_manager.py, logged, and execution continues. This creates silent data loss where the in-memory variable pool contains updated values but the database doesn't, causing data inconsistency. In the original implementation, these errors would fail the node execution and stop the workflow, providing clear feedback to users.

issues.title: ConversationVariable query missing tenant_id filter
issues.description: The SELECT against the tenant-scoped ConversationVariable table is filtered by id and conversation_id only, with no tenant_id predicate. This violates the requirement that tenant-scoped queries must include tenant_id scoping to prevent cross-tenant data access.
issues.rule_name: Database Queries Must Include tenant_id Scoping

issues.title: Missing return type annotation on __init__
issues.description: The __init__ method is missing an explicit return type annotation (e.g., "-> None"), which violates the requirement that all Python function definitions include type annotations for parameters and return values.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: def __init__(self, variables: dict[tuple[str, str], object] | None = None):
issues.rule_name: Python Functions Must Include Type Annotations

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30531 - feat: Add conversation variable persistence layer

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves conversation-variable persistence out of the Variable Assigner v1/v2 nodes and into a new `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer`. The layer listens for `NodeRunSucceededEvent` from VARIABLE_ASSIGNER nodes, reads the updated variables from `process_data`, pulls the current value from the variable pool, and calls a `ConversationVariableUpdater`. The updater implementation moves from `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py` to `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`. The node-side code is simpler and the tests now assert on `process_data` instead of mocks. The restructuring is sound, but the move changes failure semantics. Layer exceptions are swallowed by the event manager, so a failed DB write no longer fails the node, and the write itself regresses: the session is no longer closed.

The most important problems are: (1) a persistence failure now leaves the node reported as SUCCEEDED while the DB is stale; (2) `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update` opens a `Session` without a context manager, which leaks the connection on every call; and (3) a missing `conversation_id` now silently skips persistence where v2 previously raised. Test coverage for the layer's failure and missing-conversation branches is also absent.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The refactor itself is reasonable, but it introduces a silent-data-divergence risk: DB write failures are logged and swallowed by `EventManager._notify_layers` instead of failing the node. The updater also leaks a SQLAlchemy session on every write, which is a regression from the original `with Session(...)` block. Both should be fixed before merge. The missing-conversation-id skip is a behavior change that needs an explicit decision.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `VariableAssignerNode` v1 and v2 each wrote conversation variables to the database inside `_run()`, using a `ConversationVariableUpdater` injected through `conv_var_updater_factory` or a private method. A DB failure therefore failed the node, and the node result was the single source of truth for the outcome. The graph engine notifies registered layers for each event through `EventManager._notify_layers`, which catches and logs layer exceptions.

After this PR, the nodes only mutate the in-memory variable pool and emit the updated variables in `process_data`. A new `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer` is registered in `AdvancedChatAppRunner` ahead of the pause-state persistence layer. It handles `NodeRunSucceededEvent` for VARIABLE_ASSIGNER nodes, reads the conversation variables from `process_data`, looks up the live value in the variable pool, and calls `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl`, which now lives in `services/` and is also used by `conversation_service`. Persistence is now asynchronous with respect to the node's outcome and its failure handling is weaker.
steps: Entry point: `AdvancedChatAppRunner` builds the graph engine and attaches layers. The new layer is attached first, using `conversation_variable_updater_factory()` from `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`.
Nodes: `v1/node.py` and `v2/node.py` no longer touch the database. They update the pool and attach the processed variables to `process_data` via `set_updated_variables`.

Event path: when a VARIABLE_ASSIGNER node succeeds, `EventManager` notifies each layer. `_notify_layers` catches layer exceptions and only logs them, so a failure in the new layer does not change the node's status.

Persistence: the layer filters for `CONVERSATION` selectors, reads the current value from the pool, and calls `update` and `flush` on the updater. `update` opens a session, looks up the row by id and conversation id, and commits the new JSON.
Review focus: check whether losing node-level failure semantics is acceptable, and whether the session lifecycle in the updater is correct after the move.

findings.title: Persistence failures no longer fail the node; the DB silently diverges
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`, `on_event` calls `_conversation_variable_updater.update` and `flush` for each conversation variable of a VARIABLE_ASSIGNER success event. Exceptions there are swallowed by `EventManager._notify_layers` (`api/core/workflow/graph_engine/event_management/event_manager.py`), so a failed DB write leaves the node reported as SUCCEEDED while the DB stays stale. Restore the old guarantee that a persistence failure fails the assigner node or the run. Options: persist inside the node again, or have the layer send a failing command through `command_channel`. Also make the multi-variable writes atomic (one session/transaction for all updates in an event). Add a test asserting that an updater exception does not produce a silent success. Keep the public updater protocol in `core/workflow/conversation_variable_updater.py` unchanged.

findings.title: Updater opens a Session without closing it, leaking a DB connection on every write
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update` creates `session = Session(db.engine)` without a context manager, so the session and its connection are never released explicitly. The original code in `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py` used `with Session(db.engine) as session:`. Restore that pattern around the `scalar`, the not-found check, the `row.data` assignment, and `commit()`, so the session closes on both the success and the raise path. Keep the `ConversationVariableNotFoundError` behaviour. Add a unit test that the session is closed when the row is missing, for example by patching `Session` and asserting `__exit__` was called.

findings.title: Missing conversation_id now silently skips persistence instead of failing
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`, `on_event` returns silently when `system_variable.conversation_id` is None, while the old v2 node raised `ConversationIDNotFoundError` for non-debugger runs. Decide the intended behaviour. If a conversation variable is being assigned with no conversation, it should either fail loudly or be logged as a warning, matching the old v2 behaviour outside the debugger. If it is intended to be silently skipped, say so in the code comment and tests. Also remove or reuse `ConversationIDNotFoundError` in `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/exc.py`, which is now dead code. Add a layer test for the None-conversation-id path.

findings.title: Layer persists the live pool value rather than the value the node produced
findings.body:
The layer takes the variable name from `process_data`, but it writes the value it currently finds in `graph_runtime_state.variable_pool` at the time the event is dispatched. The node's own result is ignored. In the common case this is fine. But when two assigners in parallel branches touch the same conversation variable, the event for one of them can be processed after the other node has already written the pool. The DB then records whichever value the pool holds at that moment, not the value this node produced. The end state will match the pool, but it may not match the order of the events.

::code{file="api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py" lines="44-52"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`, `on_event` reads each conversation variable from the live `variable_pool` at event dispatch time, not from the `new_value` recorded in the node's `process_data`. For parallel assigners touching the same variable, this can persist a value other than the one the node produced. Build the `Variable` to persist from the node's own `process_data` (`updated_variables` items carry `new_value`) or otherwise confirm that reading the pool at dispatch time is intended. Add a test with two assigner events for the same variable to show the expected persisted value.

findings.title: Layer tests do not cover failure or missing-conversation paths; node factory test is weak
findings.body:
The new layer tests cover the happy path, the missing-outputs case, non-assigner events, and non-conversation selectors. They do not cover:

- an updater that raises (the swallow-and-continue behaviour from the first finding),
- `conversation_id is None` (the silent-skip behaviour from the third finding),
- two variables in one event (partial-failure behaviour),
- a selector shorter than 2 (the warning branch).

The added `test_node_factory_creates_variable_assigner_node` only asserts `isinstance(node, VariableAssignerNode)`. It would pass with or without the trivial `__init__` override in v2 (see the low-severity note on that override), so it adds little coverage for the change.

::code{file="api/tests/unit_tests/core/app/layers/test_conversation_variable_persist_layer.py" lines="112-144"}
findings.fixPrompt: Extend `api/tests/unit_tests/core/app/layers/test_conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` with tests for: (1) the updater's `update` raising, asserting what the layer does (currently it propagates to `EventManager`, which logs it); (2) `conversation_id=None` skipping persistence; (3) an event with two conversation variables, asserting both are updated and that `flush` is called as intended; (4) a selector shorter than two elements being skipped with a warning. Replace or drop the `isinstance`-only test in `test_variable_assigner_v2.py` that was added for the factory. Assert observable behaviour (updater calls, node status) rather than internal calls.

findings.title: Dead or no-op code left behind in v2 node and factory
findings.body:
The v2 `VariableAssignerNode.__init__` only forwards its arguments to `super().__init__` unchanged, so it has no effect. The `node_factory.py` change removes a blank line and makes no functional change. `ConversationIDNotFoundError` in `v2/exc.py` is no longer used. `ConversationVariableNotFoundError` in the updater no longer inherits from `VariableOperatorNodeError`, which changes the error contract for `conversation_service`; any caller that catches `VariableOperatorNodeError` will no longer see it.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py" lines="56-68"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py`, remove the no-op `__init__` override that only forwards its arguments to `super().__init__`, and drop the now-unused `GraphInitParams`/`GraphRuntimeState` TYPE_CHECKING imports if they become unused. Remove `ConversationIDNotFoundError` from `v2/exc.py` if nothing else references it. In `api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, decide whether `ConversationVariableNotFoundError` should subclass `VariableOperatorNodeError` for compatibility, and check callers in `api/services/conversation_service.py`. Restore the blank line removed in `api/core/workflow/nodes/node_factory.py` only if it was intentional. Then delete the test that exists only to exercise the removed `__init__`.

findings.title: Persistence moved out of nodes and into a single layer
findings.body: Moving the database write out of `_run()` is a good change. The v1 and v2 nodes now compute the result and report it in `process_data`, without side effects on the DB. That makes them easier to test, because the v1 and v2 tests now assert on `common_helpers.get_updated_variables(...)`, which is the same contract the layer uses. The `.importlinter` ignore for the old `common.impl` module is removed correctly because the module is gone, and the importer in `conversation_service.py` was updated to match.

findings.title: Read-only pool protocol now uses positional-only selector
findings.body: `ReadOnlyVariablePool.get` and `ReadOnlyVariablePoolWrapper.get` now take `selector: Sequence[str], /`, which matches `VariablePool.get` and removes the old `(node_id, variable_key)` shape. The mock in `test_pause_state_persist_layer.py` is updated to match. Any caller that passes `selector=` by keyword will break, but none appear in this diff.
